@hardware.colours.spectrum.context: Value of the Colours row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): the ZX Spectrum's 8 colours, each with a BRIGHT variant (black has none, hence 15). BRIGHT is a BASIC keyword: keep it.

@hardware.colours.monochrome.context: Value of the Colours row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): a black-and-white picture (ZX80, ZX81).

@hardware.colours.next.context: Value of the Colours row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next: up to 256 colours at once, chosen from palettes of 512 colours.

@hardware.colours.monochromeLcd.context: Value of the Colours row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Cambridge Z88, whose screen is a black-and-white liquid-crystal display.

@hardware.attributes.spectrum.context: Value of the Attributes row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): colour is set per character cell, 32 columns by 24 rows of 8 by 8 pixels, and cells can FLASH. FLASH is a BASIC keyword: keep it.

hardware.attributes.timex: 32 × 24 cells of 8 × 8 px, or 32 × 192 cells of 8 × 1 px (extended colour), FLASH

@hardware.attributes.timex.context: Value of the Attributes row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Timex machines: normal 8×8-pixel colour cells, or 8×1-pixel cells in the extended-colour mode. FLASH is a BASIC keyword: keep it.

@hardware.attributes.z88.context: Value of the Attributes row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Cambridge Z88: the per-character display effects its LCD supports (grey, inverse video, flashing, underlined).

@hardware.text.zx81.context: Value of the Text row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX81: a 32-column, 24-row character screen that the Z80 itself draws.

hardware.text.zx80: 32 × 24 characters; blank while the CPU computes

@hardware.text.zx80.context: Value of the Text row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX80: the picture disappears while a program runs, because the Z80 cannot draw it then.

@hardware.text.ht1080z.context: Value of the Text row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the HT-1080Z, a Hungarian school computer compatible with the TRS-80 Model I: a 64-column, 16-row character screen, whose characters can also be 2 × 3 blocks, giving 128 × 48 block graphics.

hardware.layers.next: ULA, Layer 2 (up to 320 × 256), tilemap, sprites, copper

@hardware.layers.next.context: Value of the Layers row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next: its display layers. ULA, Layer 2 and copper are hardware names: keep them; tilemap and sprites may be translated if your language has settled terms.

hardware.otherSizes.timex: 512 × 192 in two colours (64-column mode); a second screen at $6000

@hardware.otherSizes.timex.context: Value of the Other sizes row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Timex machines: their extra screen modes. Keep chip, port and register names, numbers, $hex values and file extensions as they are.

@hardware.otherSizes.z88.context: Value of the Other sizes row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Cambridge Z88: the LCD can be configured as 640 pixels wide by 256, 320 or 480 pixels high.

@hardware.raster.outputBuffer.context: Follows the pixel size in the Raster row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next ("720 × 288 output buffer"): the size of the picture the emulator renders, not of the TV picture. Lowercase.

@hardware.turbo.next.context: Value of the Turbo row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next: the CPU speeds it can run at, chosen by a hardware register. Keep chip, port and register names, numbers, $hex values and file extensions as they are.

hardware.addressSpace.timex2068: 64K as eight 8K chunks, each HOME, DOCK or EXROM (port $F4)

@hardware.addressSpace.timex2068.context: Value of the Address space row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the TC2068/TS2068: the 64K memory map is split into eight 8K chunks, each mapped to one of three memory banks. HOME, DOCK and EXROM are bank names: keep them. Keep chip, port and register names, numbers, $hex values and file extensions as they are.

hardware.timing.timexNtsc: 60 Hz at the SCLD's 3.528 MHz; port $FF bit 6 holds off the frame interrupt

@hardware.timing.timexNtsc.context: Note under the frame timing in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the TS2068 (the American model). SCLD is the Timex video chip: keep it. Keep chip, port and register names, numbers, $hex values and file extensions as they are.

hardware.timing.timexPal: The 48K's raster at the SCLD's 3.528 MHz; port $FF bit 6 holds off the frame interrupt

@hardware.timing.timexPal.context: Note under the frame timing in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the European Timex machines: the same picture timing as the ZX Spectrum 48K, at a slightly different clock. SCLD is the Timex video chip: keep it. Keep chip, port and register names, numbers, $hex values and file extensions as they are.

hardware.timing.pentagon: No memory or I/O contention and no floating bus; the 128K ROMs

@hardware.timing.pentagon.context: Note under the frame timing in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Pentagon (a Russian Spectrum clone): unlike the Sinclair machines, it never slows the CPU down when it touches video memory or ports, and it has no floating bus; it runs the 128K's ROMs. "Contention" and "floating bus" are established Spectrum terms.

hardware.timing.scorpion: No memory or I/O contention; $1FFD adds RAM at $0000, the service ROM and banks 8-15

@hardware.timing.scorpion.context: Note under the frame timing in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Scorpion ZS-256 (a Russian Spectrum clone): no memory or port contention, and what its extra paging port $1FFD switches in. Keep chip, port and register names, numbers, $hex values and file extensions as they are.

hardware.timing.next: Frame timing follows the video mode (48K, 128K/+3, Pentagon) and 50/60 Hz, set by NextRegs $03 and $05.

@hardware.timing.next.context: Note in the timing section of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next, which has no single frame timing. Keep chip, port and register names, numbers, $hex values and file extensions as they are.

hardware.timing.ht1080z: One T-state per character position; no interrupts

@hardware.timing.ht1080z.context: Value of the Timing note row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the HT-1080Z, a Hungarian school computer compatible with the TRS-80 Model I: the video circuit draws one character position for every clock cycle (T-state) of the Z80 processor, and the machine has no interrupt source. Keep "T-state", the Z80 term for one clock cycle.

hardware.rom.timexHome: HOME ROM; your copy, or the 48K ROM

@hardware.rom.timexHome.context: Role of a ROM image in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) (after the file name and size) for the TC2068/TS2068: the main ROM, taken from the user's own ROM file, or the ZX Spectrum 48K ROM when they have none. HOME is a bank name: keep it.

@hardware.rom.timexExrom.context: Role of a ROM image in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the TC2068/TS2068: the extension ROM, read from the same file as the HOME ROM. EXROM is a bank name: keep it.

hardware.rom.tc2048: your copy; the 48K ROM without one

@hardware.rom.tc2048.context: Role of a ROM image in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the TC2048: the user's own ROM file is used, or the ZX Spectrum 48K ROM when they have none. Lowercase.

@hardware.rom.editor128.context: Role of a ROM image in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): the ROM page holding the ZX Spectrum 128's menu and full-screen BASIC editor. Lowercase.

@hardware.rom.basic48.context: Role of a ROM image in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): the ROM page holding the original ZX Spectrum 48K BASIC.

@hardware.rom.scorpionEditor.context: Role of the Scorpion's first ROM page in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): the 128K menu and editor, from the user's own ROM file, or the ZX Spectrum 128's ROM when they have none. Lowercase.

@hardware.rom.scorpionBasic.context: Role of the Scorpion's second ROM page in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): 48K BASIC, from the user's own ROM file, or the ZX Spectrum 128's ROM when they have none.

@hardware.rom.scorpionService.context: Role of the Scorpion's third ROM page in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): a machine-code monitor for servicing, only from the user's own ROM file. Lowercase.

hardware.rom.scorpionTrdos: TR-DOS; your ROM, or the TR-DOS ROM file

@hardware.rom.scorpionTrdos.context: Role of the Scorpion's fourth ROM page in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): the TR-DOS disk system, from the user's own ROM file, or from the separate TR-DOS ROM file. TR-DOS is a product name: keep it.

@hardware.rom.nextRoms.context: Role of a ROM image in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next: the file holding its main ROM pages.

@hardware.rom.alternative.context: Role of a ROM image in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next: a second ROM the machine can switch to. Lowercase.

@hardware.rom.characterSet.context: Role of a ROM image in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Commodore 64: the ROM holding the character shapes. Lowercase.

@hardware.rom.htBasic.context: Value of the ROM row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the HT-1080Z, a Hungarian school computer compatible with the TRS-80 Model I: the role of the 12K ROM that holds the BASIC interpreter. Level II BASIC is the name of the TRS-80 BASIC (by Microsoft): keep "Level II".

@hardware.rom.htExtension.context: Value of the ROM row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the HT-1080Z, a Hungarian school computer compatible with the TRS-80 Model I: the role of the 2K ROM that adds commands and keyboard features to the BASIC.

@hardware.rom.ozFlash.context: Role of the Cambridge Z88's internal ROM in the ROM row of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) when it sits in a flash chip. OZ is the Z88's operating system: keep it.

placeholders.cardType: The flash chip type, e.g. AMD or Intel (a chip family name, not translated)

@hardware.sound.beeper.context: An item of the Sound row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): the simple one-bit speaker of the Spectrum and Z88. Keep the English word if your language uses it for this.

@hardware.sound.ayTimex.context: An item of the Sound row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the TC2068/TS2068: the AY sound chip and the ports it is reached through. Keep chip, port and register names, numbers, $hex values and file extensions as they are.

hardware.sound.ayHt1080z: AY-3-8910 PSG at the CPU clock (ports $1E/$1F), mono

@hardware.sound.ayHt1080z.context: An item of the Sound row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the HT-1080Z: its AY sound chip, which runs from the processor's clock and whose three channels are mixed into one. Keep chip, port and register names, numbers, $hex values and file extensions as they are.

@hardware.sound.nextDac.context: An item of the Sound row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next: its four-channel digital-to-analogue converter, compatible with the SpecDrum. SpecDrum is a product name: keep it.

@hardware.media.spectrumTape.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): the machine loads programs from tape, from TAP and TZX tape-image files.

@hardware.media.timexCartridge.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the TC2068/TS2068: a cartridge image (.dck file) plugged into the DOCK slot. DOCK is a bank name: keep it.

hardware.media.pentagonBeta: Beta 128: 2 drives (TRD, SCL), with your TR-DOS ROM

@hardware.media.pentagonBeta.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Pentagon: the Beta 128 disk interface with two floppy drives (TRD and SCL disk images), which boots the user's own TR-DOS ROM. Beta 128 and TR-DOS are product names: keep them.

@hardware.media.scorpionBeta.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Scorpion: a built-in Beta 128 disk interface with two floppy drives (TRD and SCL disk images). Beta 128 is a product name: keep it.

@hardware.media.sdCard.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next: it boots from an SD card, emulated by a FAT32 disk-image file.

@hardware.media.z88Cards.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Cambridge Z88: its three card slots, which take RAM, EPROM and flash cards.

@hardware.media.zx81Tape.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX81: it loads programs from tape, from .P files.

@hardware.media.ht1080zTape.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the HT-1080Z: the file types its tape deck takes. Keep the file extensions as they are.

@hardware.media.zx80Tape.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX80: it loads programs from tape, from .O files.

@hardware.media.tape.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts), and a short tag (chip) in the dialog's machine list: the machine loads programs from a cassette tape.

@hardware.media.noFloppy.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for a +2A/+3/+3E model without a floppy drive.

@hardware.media.floppyA.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): one floppy drive, A:, which takes DSK disk images.

hardware.media.floppyAB: Floppy disk drives A and B (DSK)

@hardware.media.floppyAB.context: An item of the Media row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): two floppy drives, A: and B:, which take DSK disk images.

@hardware.chip.cartridge.context: A short tag (chip) under a machine model's name in the Select Machine dialog, naming one of its storage media. Keep it short. Here: a cartridge slot.

@hardware.chip.beta128.context: A short tag (chip) under a machine model's name in the Select Machine dialog, naming one of its storage media. Keep it short. Here: the Beta 128 disk interface with two floppy drives. Beta 128 is a product name: keep it.

@hardware.chip.sdCard.context: A short tag (chip) under a machine model's name in the Select Machine dialog, naming one of its storage media. Keep it short. Here: the ZX Spectrum Next's SD card.

@hardware.chip.z88Cards.context: A short tag (chip) under a machine model's name in the Select Machine dialog, naming one of its storage media. Keep it short. Here: the Cambridge Z88's three card slots.

@hardware.chip.floppyA.context: A short tag (chip) under a machine model's name in the Select Machine dialog, naming one of its storage media. Keep it short. Here: one floppy drive, A:.

hardware.chip.floppyAB: Floppy disk drives A and B

@hardware.chip.floppyAB.context: A short tag (chip) under a machine model's name in the Select Machine dialog, naming one of its storage media. Keep it short. Here: two floppy drives, A: and B:.

@hardware.input.keyboard.context: Label of a row in the input-devices part of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts).

@hardware.input.joystick.context: Label of a row in the input-devices part of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts). One joystick.

@hardware.input.joysticks.context: Label of a row in the input-devices part of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts). More than one joystick.

@hardware.input.mouse.context: Label of a row in the input-devices part of the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts).

@hardware.keyboard.spectrum.context: Value of the Keyboard row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts): the ZX Spectrum's 40-key keyboard.

@hardware.keyboard.zx8081.context: Value of the Keyboard row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX80/ZX81: a flat 40-key membrane keyboard.

@hardware.keyboard.ht1080z.context: Value of the Keyboard row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the HT-1080Z, a Hungarian school computer compatible with the TRS-80 Model I: a full-travel keyboard laid out as the TRS-80 Model I's. TRS-80 is a product name: keep it.

@hardware.keyboard.next.context: Value of the Keyboard row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next: its own keyboard, which has keys the original Spectrum lacks.

@hardware.keyboard.z88.context: Value of the Keyboard row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the Cambridge Z88.

placeholders.layout: The keyboard's national layout, e.g. UK, German or Swedish/Finnish (one of the hardware.keyboard.layout.* texts)

@hardware.keyboard.layout.uk.context: The national layout of a Cambridge Z88 keyboard, inserted into "64 keys, {layout} layout" in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts). The British layout.

@hardware.keyboard.layout.de.context: The national layout of a Cambridge Z88 keyboard, inserted into "64 keys, {layout} layout" in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts).

@hardware.keyboard.layout.fr.context: The national layout of a Cambridge Z88 keyboard, inserted into "64 keys, {layout} layout" in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts).

@hardware.keyboard.layout.es.context: The national layout of a Cambridge Z88 keyboard, inserted into "64 keys, {layout} layout" in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts).

@hardware.keyboard.layout.it.context: The national layout of a Cambridge Z88 keyboard, inserted into "64 keys, {layout} layout" in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts).

@hardware.keyboard.layout.dk.context: The national layout of a Cambridge Z88 keyboard, inserted into "64 keys, {layout} layout" in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts).

@hardware.keyboard.layout.se.context: The national layout of a Cambridge Z88 keyboard, inserted into "64 keys, {layout} layout" in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts). One layout shared by Sweden and Finland.

@hardware.joystick.timex2068.context: Value of the Joysticks row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the TC2068/TS2068: two joystick ports, read through the AY sound chip's I/O port. AY is a chip name: keep it.

@hardware.joystick.timexKempston.context: Value of the Joystick row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the TC2048: a built-in Kempston-compatible joystick port. Kempston is a product name: keep it.

@hardware.joystick.nextPorts.context: Value of the Joysticks row in the hardware sheet of the Select Machine dialog (a two-column table of a machine model's facts) for the ZX Spectrum Next: two joystick ports.
